en: female in-law (the mother of your child's spouse)

examples.ko: 아들 결혼식 날 안사돈을 처음 만났어요.
examples.en: I met my son's mother-in-law for the first time on the wedding day.
Tomorrow I'm having a meal with my child's in-law.
My mother sent a gift directly to the other in-law, my child's mother-in-law's side.
My child's mother-in-law made a lot of kimchi for us.
I find myself careful with my words in front of my child's in-law.
My daughter's mother-in-law is my in-law.

explain: 사돈 중에서 여자 쪽, 곧 자녀 배우자의 어머니를 가리켜요. 남자 쪽은 '바깥사돈'이라고 해서 짝으로 쓰지만, 실제로는 그냥 '사돈'이라고 많이 불러요. 결혼식이나 가족 모임 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the female side of the in-laws, that is, the mother of your child's spouse. Its counterpart is '바깥사돈' (the male in-law), but in practice people often just say '사돈'. It comes up in talk about weddings and family gatherings.

examples.en: My wife prepared dinner tonight.
I'll ask my wife and then give you an answer.
My wife is from Seoul.

examples.ko: 주말에 안사람과 같이 여행을 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: I'm going on a trip with my wife this weekend.

examples.ko: 안사람이 요즘 일이 바빠서 늦게 와요.
examples.en: My wife is busy with work these days, so she comes home late.

examples.ko: 안사람 생일이라 오늘은 일찍 들어가 볼게요.
examples.en: It's my wife's birthday, so I'll head home early today.

explain: 남자가 다른 사람에게 자기 아내를 낮춰서 말할 때 써요. 남의 아내를 말할 때는 쓰지 않고 '부인', '사모님'을 써요. 요즘 젊은 사람들은 '아내', '와이프'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: A man uses it humbly when speaking about his own wife to others. You don't use it for someone else's wife; say '부인' or '사모님' instead. These days younger people more often say '아내' or '와이프'.

examples.ko: 어머니가 안살림을 잘하셔서 집이 늘 깨끗해요.
examples.en: My mother manages the household well, so our home is always clean.

examples.ko: 우리 집 안살림은 아내가 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: My wife is in charge of the household at our home.

examples.ko: 새로 온 며느리가 안살림을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: The new daughter-in-law is learning how to run the household.
That family runs its household very thriftily.
These days more husbands help even with the household work.

examples.ko: 바깥일은 남편이, 안살림은 아내가 나눠서 했어요.
examples.en: The husband handled outside work, and the wife handled the household.

explain: 집 안에서 하는 살림을 뜻하고, 집 밖의 일인 '바깥일'과 짝을 이뤄요. 요즘 대화에서는 '집안일'이나 그냥 '살림'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 옛날식 느낌이 있어서 가족 이야기나 글에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It means the housekeeping done inside the home and pairs with '바깥일' (work outside the home). In everyday talk people more often say '집안일' or just '살림'. It has an old-fashioned feel and shows up in stories about family and in writing.

examples.en: If a company falls into complacency, it's hard for it to grow.
The boss is very worried about the employees' complacency.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 안일주의 때문에 큰 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: That team made a big mistake because of its take-it-easy attitude.

examples.ko: 이제 안일주의를 버리고 새로운 방법을 찾아봐요.
examples.en: Let's drop the complacency and look for a new method.

examples.ko: 공무원 사회의 안일주의를 비판하는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article criticizing the complacency in the civil service.
We have to be careful not to let complacency spread.

explain: 어렵거나 힘든 일은 피하고 편한 쪽만 택하는 태도를 비판할 때 써요. '무사안일주의'라고도 하고, 회의나 뉴스처럼 조금 딱딱한 자리에서 나와요. 보통 '안일주의에 빠지다', '안일주의를 버리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used to criticize an attitude of avoiding hard things and choosing only what is easy. It is also said as '무사안일주의' and appears in somewhat formal settings like meetings and the news. Typical patterns are '안일주의에 빠지다' and '안일주의를 버리다'.

examples.ko: 저는 현장에 가기 전에 안전모와 안전화를 챙겼어요.
examples.en: Before going to the site, I packed a hard hat and safety shoes.
You must wear safety shoes at a construction site.
The safety shoes were heavy, so walking was hard at first.

examples.ko: 새 안전화를 사려고 작업복 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a workwear shop to buy new safety shoes.
My father tied his safety shoe laces tightly.

examples.ko: 안전화 앞부분이 단단해서 발을 보호해 줘요.
examples.en: The front of safety shoes is hard, so they protect your feet.

explain: 공사장이나 공장에서 발을 다치지 않게 신는 작업용 신발이에요. 보통 '안전모'와 같이 말하고, 동사는 '신다'를 써요. 일반 운동화와는 달리 일할 때 꼭 필요한 장비로 생각해요.
explain_en: These are work shoes worn at construction sites or factories to protect your feet. It is often mentioned together with '안전모' (hard hat), and the verb is '신다' (to wear on the feet). Unlike regular sneakers, they are seen as required gear for work.

examples.en: With this exam score, you're safely within passing range.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이미 우승 안정권에 들었어요.
examples.en: Our team is already safely in range of winning the title.
I'm glad prices have settled into a stable range.

examples.ko: 안정권에 들려면 몇 점 더 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To get into the safe range, you need a few more points.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 제 성적으로 안정권이 아니에요.
examples.en: That school is not a safe bet with my grades.
They say the exchange rate has returned to a stable range.

explain: 입시나 스포츠 뉴스에서 '합격 안정권', '우승 안정권'처럼 많이 써요. '들다', '들어서다'와 자주 같이 나오고, 마음 놓아도 될 만한 수준이라는 느낌이에요. 가격이나 환율처럼 수치가 안정된 범위를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is common in admissions and sports news, as in '합격 안정권' (safe range for admission) or '우승 안정권'. It often goes with '들다' or '들어서다' and gives the feeling that you can relax. It can also describe numbers like prices or exchange rates staying in a stable range.

examples.en: The doctor prescribed me a sedative.
I was so nervous that I wanted to take a tranquilizer.
This medicine is a tranquilizer that calms the mind.
Is it okay to give a puppy a calming medicine?

examples.ko: 안정제 때문에 졸려서 운전을 못 해요.
examples.en: The sedative makes me sleepy, so I can't drive.
After I took a tranquilizer, I felt a little calmer.

explain: 마음을 가라앉히는 약을 말할 때는 '진정제', '신경안정제'와 거의 같은 자리에서 써요. 약 말고도 식품이나 화학 제품에서 상태를 일정하게 유지해 주는 재료를 말할 때도 있어요. 병원이나 약 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: For medicine that calms the mind, it is used in much the same places as '진정제' and '신경안정제'. Besides drugs, it can also mean an ingredient in food or chemical products that keeps things in a steady state. You'll hear it in talk about hospitals and medicine.

en: main house; inner quarters of a hanok

examples.en: The guests had dinner in the main building.
Grandmother lives in the inner house and my uncle in the guest quarters.
The main building of that hanok is very spacious.
I passed the gate and went into the main house.

examples.ko: 안채 마루에 앉아 비 오는 마당을 구경했어요.
examples.en: I sat on the wooden floor of the main house and watched the rainy yard.

examples.ko: 안채와 사랑채 사이에 작은 마당이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small yard between the main house and the guest quarters.

explain: 한옥에서 가족이 주로 생활하는 중심 건물이에요. 손님을 맞는 '사랑채'와 짝으로 자주 말해요. 요즘은 한옥 마을이나 옛날이야기, 드라마에서 많이 만나요.
explain_en: In a hanok (traditional house), it is the central building where the family mainly lives. It is often paired with '사랑채', where guests are received. Today you meet it mostly in hanok villages, old stories and dramas.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 돈이 좀 있다고 안하무인으로 굴어요.
examples.en: He acts arrogantly just because he has a bit of money.

examples.ko: 안하무인인 손님 때문에 직원이 많이 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: The staff had a hard time because of an arrogant customer.
Everyone got angry at his arrogant attitude.
I was shocked that my senior acted as if no one else mattered.
He has been insolent since he was a child.
Insolent behavior doesn't look good.

explain: 남을 안중에도 두지 않고 건방지게 구는 모습을 말해요. '건방지다'보다 훨씬 강하고 한자성어 같은 느낌이라, 말할 때는 '안하무인이다', '안하무인으로 굴다'처럼 써요. 좋은 뜻으로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It describes behaving insolently with no regard for other people. It is much stronger than '건방지다' and feels like a four-character idiom; common patterns are '안하무인이다' and '안하무인으로 굴다'. It is never used in a positive sense.

examples.en: My sitting height is tall, so chairs are uncomfortable.
We are about the same height, but our sitting heights differ.

examples.ko: 앉은키를 재려면 벽에 등을 대고 앉으세요.
examples.en: To measure your sitting height, sit with your back against the wall.

examples.ko: 아이의 앉은키에 맞게 책상 높이를 정했어요.
examples.en: I set the desk height to fit my child's sitting height.

examples.ko: 앉은키가 작아서 극장에서 앞이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: My sitting height is short, so I can't see the front well in a theater.

examples.ko: 형은 키는 작은데 앉은키는 저보다 커요.
examples.en: My brother is shorter, but his sitting height is greater than mine.

explain: 의자에 앉았을 때 의자 면에서 머리끝까지의 높이예요. 서 있을 때의 키는 그냥 '키'라고 하고, 다리가 긴 사람은 키에 비해 앉은키가 작게 느껴져요. 건강검진이나 의자·책상을 고를 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is the height from the seat or floor to the top of your head when sitting. Standing height is simply '키', and people with long legs have a smaller sitting height relative to their height. It comes up in health checkups and when choosing chairs or desks.

en: person with no property at all; penniless person

examples.en: His business failed and he became penniless overnight.
He came up to Seoul with absolutely nothing.
I almost lost everything because of stocks.
Once I was left penniless, my friends disappeared too.
Before payday I'm practically broke.

examples.ko: 잘못된 투자로 재산을 날려 알거지가 된 사람 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about a man who lost his fortune in a bad investment and ended up penniless.

explain: 가진 것이 하나도 없는 사람을 말해요. '빈털터리'와 비슷하지만 '거지'가 들어가서 더 센 표현이에요. 월급날 전에 '나 알거지야'처럼 과장해서 농담으로도 써요.
explain_en: It means a person with absolutely nothing. It is similar to '빈털터리' but stronger because it contains '거지' (beggar). People also joke with it, saying '나 알거지야' before payday.

examples.en: He only fawns when he is in front of the boss.
Stop sucking up and tell me honestly.

examples.ko: 후배가 선배에게 알랑거리는 모습이 보기 싫었어요.
examples.en: I disliked seeing the junior suck up to the senior.
Why are you suddenly buttering me up?
Some people flatter their boss to get promoted.
My younger sibling schmoozed to get some pocket money.

explain: 자기에게 이익이 되도록 남에게 비위를 맞추며 아첨하는 모습이에요. 부정적인 느낌이고, '아부하다'보다 입말에 가까워요. '알랑대다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요.
explain_en: It describes flattering someone to win their favor for your own benefit. It sounds negative and is more colloquial than '아부하다'. It means the same as '알랑대다'.

examples.ko: 그 직원은 부장님 옆에서 늘 알랑대요.
examples.en: That employee is always sucking up beside the manager.
It's hard to trust people who fawn.
My friend buttered me up and then asked a favor.
It's no use sucking up to me.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마한테 알랑대며 장난감을 사 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The child coaxed his mom with sweet talk to buy him a toy.
The fawning way he spoke to customers sounded awkward.

explain: '알랑거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. '-대다'는 같은 행동을 자꾸 하는 느낌이 있어서 말할 때 더 자연스러워요. 상대를 낮게 보거나 흉볼 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '알랑거리다', so you can swap them. The '-대다' ending gives a feel of repeating the action, which sounds natural in speech. It is often used when looking down on someone or criticizing them.

examples.en: The baby runs around the yard with nothing on.

examples.ko: 털을 다 깎인 양이 알몸뚱이가 돼서 추워 보였어요.
examples.en: The sheep, with all its wool sheared off, looked cold and bare.

examples.ko: 빚 때문에 모든 걸 잃고 알몸뚱이로 시작했어요.
examples.en: I lost everything because of debt and started again with nothing.

examples.ko: 겨울 나무는 잎이 다 떨어져 알몸뚱이 같아요.
examples.en: Winter trees look bare with all their leaves fallen.
You'll catch a cold if you go out with nothing on!

examples.ko: 그림 속 아이는 알몸뚱이인데도 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The child in the picture is smiling even though he has nothing on.

explain: '알몸'을 입말로 조금 세게, 또는 정답게 말하는 표현이에요. 보통은 '알몸'이 기본이고, '알몸뚱이'는 옛이야기나 만화, 말투에 감정이 들어갈 때 잘 보여요. 옷뿐 아니라 가진 게 아무것도 없는 상태를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a more colloquial, stronger or sometimes affectionate way to say '알몸' (naked body). '알몸' is the standard word, while '알몸뚱이' shows up in old tales, comics and emotional speech. It can also figuratively mean having nothing at all, not just no clothes.

examples.en: Unlike how he looks, that old man is actually very rich.
He is rumored to be a quietly wealthy man in the neighborhood.
Even though he is truly wealthy, he only wears worn clothes.
I heard the man next door is secretly rich.

examples.ko: 작은 가게로 알부자가 된 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people have grown rich with a small shop.

examples.ko: 알부자 소리를 들어도 늘 절약하며 살아요.
examples.en: Even though people call him rich, he always lives frugally.

explain: 겉으로는 평범해 보여도 실제로는 재산이 많은 사람을 말해요. 크게 자랑하지 않는 부자라는 느낌이 있어서 보통 따뜻하게 또는 부러운 마음으로 말해요. '그 가게 사장님은 알부자래요'처럼 남의 소문을 전할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means someone who looks ordinary but actually has a lot of wealth. It suggests a rich person who doesn't show off, and is usually said warmly or with envy. People often use it when passing along gossip, like '그 가게 사장님은 알부자래요'.

examples.en: I can't quite tell what the answer to this question is.
It was puzzling what his words meant.
He looked at me with a puzzled expression.
The name is on the tip of my tongue, but I can't recall it.
If you're unsure, ask the teacher.
I barely solved the puzzling riddle.

explain: '헷갈리다'는 비슷한 둘이 섞여 구분이 안 될 때 쓰고, '알쏭달쏭하다'는 답이나 뜻이 잡힐 듯 말 듯 분명하지 않을 때 써요. '아리송하다'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. '알쏭달쏭한 표정', '알쏭달쏭한 수수께끼'처럼 사람의 표정이나 문제를 꾸미는 말로도 써요.
explain_en: '헷갈리다' is for when two similar things get mixed up and you cannot tell them apart. '알쏭달쏭하다' is for when an answer or meaning is almost within reach but still unclear. It can be swapped with '아리송하다'. It also modifies a look or a problem, as in '알쏭달쏭한 표정' or '알쏭달쏭한 수수께끼'.

examples.en: I got introduced to a good house through connections.
The word spread from person to person and customers increased.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 알음알음 찾아오는 단골이 많아요.
examples.en: That shop has many regulars who come by word of acquaintance.

examples.ko: 알음알음 알게 된 사이라서 서로 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: We got to know each other through acquaintances, so we don't know each other well.

examples.ko: 이 모임은 알음알음 사람이 모여서 커졌어요.
examples.en: This group grew as people gathered through personal connections.
It was a job I found through connections, so there was no contract.

explain: 광고 없이 아는 사람을 통해 이어지고 퍼지는 방식을 말해요. '입소문'은 소문이 퍼지는 것이고, '알음알음'은 사람의 인맥을 따라가는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '알음알음으로', '알음알음 알게 되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It describes things spreading or connecting through people you know, without advertising. '입소문' is about word spreading, while '알음알음' strongly suggests following personal connections. Typical uses are '알음알음으로' and '알음알음 알게 되다'.

en: the cream; quintessence; the best part

examples.ko: 이 책에는 알짜 정보만 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: This book contains only the really valuable information.

examples.ko: 알짜 회사는 눈에 잘 안 띄어요.
examples.en: The truly solid companies don't stand out easily.
There are many top-quality shops in that market.
The really good listings sell quickly.
I picked out only the best items at the mart.
This lecture is packed with the essentials.

explain: 겉보다 속이 꽉 차고 가치 있는 것을 말해요. '알짜 정보', '알짜 회사'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 일이 많고, 같은 뜻의 '알짜배기'는 입말에 더 가까워요. 비유로 알맹이 없는 것은 '쭉정이'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to something solid and valuable on the inside, not just in appearance. It is often placed before another noun, as in '알짜 정보' or '알짜 회사', and the similar '알짜배기' is more colloquial. Figuratively, something with no substance is called '쭉정이'.

examples.ko: 이 동네 알짜배기 땅은 이미 다 팔렸어요.
examples.en: The best land in this neighborhood has already been sold.
I picked only the best items at the market.

examples.ko: 알짜배기 정보는 직접 발품을 팔아야 얻어요.
examples.en: You get the really useful info only by legwork yourself.
That shop is known as the best in the neighborhood.
I'm so envious that you landed a job at a really solid company.
I'll tell you where the good stuff is.

explain: '알짜'와 같은 뜻인데 '-배기'가 붙어서 더 입말다워요. 그냥 좋은 것이 아니라 가장 실속 있고 쓸 만한 부분을 가리켜요. 부동산, 정보, 가게 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It means the same as '알짜' but sounds more colloquial with '-배기'. It points to the most substantial and useful part, not just something good. You often hear it in talk about real estate, information and shops.

examples.en: I've been laid up in bed with a cold for several days.

examples.ko: 어머니가 갑자기 앓아누우셔서 제가 집안일을 했어요.
examples.en: My mother suddenly fell ill and took to bed, so I did the housework.
I overworked myself and ended up bedridden.
I went to visit my friend who was sick in bed.
I got sick in bed right after the exam ended.
Rest a bit before you fall ill.

explain: '아프다'보다 훨씬 심해서 자리에 누울 정도로 앓는다는 느낌이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '앓아누워요', '앓아누웠어요'로 바뀌어요. 비슷한 말로 '몸져눕다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It feels much stronger than '아프다', as in being so ill that you take to your bed. It is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so it becomes '앓아누워요' and '앓아누웠어요'. A similar word is '몸져눕다'.

examples.en: Be careful of people who sell tickets illegally.
The police are cracking down on illegal black-market dealing.

examples.ko: 암거래로 산 물건은 가짜일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Items bought through underground dealing can be fake.
The black-market price is much higher than the list price.

examples.ko: 전쟁 때는 쌀 암거래가 많았다고 해요.
examples.en: They say there was a lot of rice black-marketing during the war.
Underground dealing is increasing online, which is a problem.

explain: 법이나 규칙을 어기고 몰래 하는 거래예요. 그냥 '거래'는 중립적이지만 '암거래'는 불법이라는 뜻이 들어 있어요. 뉴스에서 '암거래를 단속하다', '암거래 가격'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is trade done secretly, breaking laws or rules. Plain '거래' is neutral, but '암거래' carries the sense of illegality. In the news you often see '암거래를 단속하다' and '암거래 가격'.

examples.en: My future looks so bleak that I can't sleep.
There is a lot of news saying the job market looks bleak.

examples.ko: 갑자기 해고 통보를 받고 눈앞이 암담했어요.
examples.en: I was suddenly told I was fired, and everything looked hopeless.
After hearing the news, my heart sank into gloom.

examples.ko: 암담한 현실 속에서도 희망을 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: I didn't let go of hope even in the bleak reality.
I have no money or job, so I feel completely hopeless.

explain: '막막하다'와 비슷하지만, '암담하다'는 어둡고 희망이 안 보이는 느낌이 더 커요. '앞날이', '현실이', '전망이'와 자주 같이 써요. 이야기할 때보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '막막하다', but '암담하다' leans more toward darkness and no hope in sight. It often goes with '앞날이' (the future), '현실이' (reality) and '전망이' (outlook). It appears more in writing and the news than in casual talk.

examples.ko: 아이가 시 암송 대회에서 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: My child won a prize at the poem recitation contest.

examples.ko: 암송을 잘하려면 소리 내어 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: To recite well, try reading aloud.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 아침 암송 연습을 해요.
examples.en: I practice reciting every morning.

examples.ko: 할머니가 하시던 기도문 암송을 들으며 자랐어요.
examples.en: I grew up hearing my grandmother recite her prayers.
I'm worried because I have a recitation assignment due tomorrow.
This poem is a good length for reciting.

explain: 외운 글을 보지 않고 소리 내어 말하는 것을 말해요. 그냥 머릿속에 넣는 일은 '외우기'라고 하고, '암송'은 시, 기도문, 구절을 말해서 들려주는 상황에서 많이 써요. 수업이나 대회, 종교 모임에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It means saying aloud from memory a text you have learned. Simply memorizing is '외우기', while '암송' is used when you speak out a poem, prayer or passage. You'll often hear it in classes, contests and religious gatherings.

examples.en: The students recite a poem in the classroom.

examples.ko: 저는 그 시를 처음부터 끝까지 암송할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can recite that poem from beginning to end.

examples.ko: 선생님이 앞에 나와서 암송해 보라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us to come to the front and recite.
The child reciting the multiplication table was cute.

examples.ko: 어제 외운 문장을 친구 앞에서 암송했어요.
examples.en: I recited the sentences I memorized yesterday in front of my friend.
I attend a group where we recite Bible verses.

explain: '외우다'는 머릿속에 기억하는 일이고, '암송하다'는 외운 것을 소리 내어 말하는 일까지 포함해요. 그래서 시, 구구단, 기도문처럼 말해서 들려주는 것에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '외워서 말하다'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: '외우다' is about fixing something in memory, while '암송하다' includes saying it aloud. So it suits things you say for others to hear, like poems, the multiplication table or prayers. In everyday talk people also say '외워서 말하다'.

examples.en: There is one pistil in the middle of the flower.
I compared the shapes of the pistil and stamens.
Bees carry pollen to the pistil.

examples.ko: 암술 끝에 꽃가루가 붙으면 열매를 맺어요.
examples.en: When pollen sticks to the tip of the pistil, the plant bears fruit.

examples.ko: 이 꽃은 암술이 길고 수술이 짧아요.
examples.en: In this flower, the pistil is long and the stamens are short.
In science class I drew a pistil.

explain: 꽃의 가운데에서 열매와 씨를 만드는 쪽을 말해요. 꽃가루를 만드는 '수술'과 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요. 주로 과학 수업이나 식물 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: It is the part at the center of a flower that goes on to form the fruit and seeds. It is easy to remember as a pair with '수술' (stamen), which makes pollen. It mainly appears in science class and talk about plants.

examples.en: They say rice was sold on the black market after the war.
Goods bought on the black market are hard to trust.

examples.ko: 그 나라에서는 암시장 환율이 훨씬 높아요.
examples.en: In that country the black-market exchange rate is much higher.
When the black market grows, the government cracks down.
My grandfather told me stories about the black market.
Lots of fake goods circulate on the black market.

explain: 법으로 허용되지 않은 방식으로 물건이나 돈이 오가는 시장이에요. 꼭 건물이 있는 시장만이 아니라 '암시장 환율'처럼 불법으로 거래되는 흐름 전체를 말하기도 해요. 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a market where goods or money change hands in ways the law does not permit. It isn't only a physical place; it can also mean the whole flow of illegal trade, as in '암시장 환율' (black-market exchange rate). It often appears in news and history stories.

en: being secretly; being covertly; being implicitly

examples.en: That plan was being carried out secretly.

examples.ko: 암암리에 소문이 퍼져서 모두 알고 있었어요.
examples.en: The rumor spread quietly, and everyone already knew.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 암암리에 약속을 했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the two companies made a secret agreement.

examples.ko: 학생들은 암암리에 서로 눈치를 보고 있어요.
examples.en: The students are quietly watching each other's reactions.
That kind of rule is being followed without anyone saying so.
There was someone who helped behind the scenes.

explain: 거의 항상 '암암리에' 형태로 쓰고, 공개하지 않고 조용히 또는 말없이 이루어지는 일에 써요. '몰래'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에 더 어울려요. 나쁜 일뿐 아니라 말없이 모두가 따르는 규칙에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '암암리에', for things done quietly or without being openly stated. It is stiffer than '몰래', so it fits the news and writing better. It can describe not only secret wrongdoing but also unspoken rules everyone follows.

examples.en: The team is groping in the dark for a solution.

examples.ko: 긴 암중모색 끝에 새로운 길을 찾았어요.
examples.en: After a long search without clear clues, we found a new way.

examples.ko: 정부도 대책을 못 찾고 암중모색만 하고 있어요.
examples.en: Even the government can't find a measure and is only feeling its way.
The months of groping around have finally ended.

examples.ko: 회사는 아직 암중모색 단계라 발표할 게 없어요.
examples.en: The company is still in the groping stage, so there's nothing to announce.
The period of feeling your way in the dark is the hardest.

explain: 뚜렷한 단서나 방법이 없는 상태에서 이것저것 시도하며 답을 찾는다는 뜻의 한자성어예요. '암중모색 중이다', '암중모색 끝에'처럼 쓰고 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '더듬더듬 찾다', '이것저것 해 보다'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom describes trying this and that to find an answer when there are no clear clues or methods. It is used in patterns like '암중모색 중이다' and '암중모색 끝에', mostly in news and writing. In daily talk people might say '더듬더듬 찾다' or '이것저것 해 보다' instead.

examples.en: These days I'm feeling my way toward a career path.

examples.ko: 여러 방법을 암중모색해 봤지만 답이 없었어요.
examples.en: We tried groping around with several methods, but found no answer.
The company searched blindly for a way to revive.
The players are feeling their way toward a new tactic.
Time just passed while everyone was groping around.
Don't be impatient when you're groping for a solution.

explain: '암중모색'에 '-하다'가 붙은 형태로, 확실한 길이 보이지 않는 상태에서 이것저것 시도하며 찾는 모습이에요. '찾다'보다 막막하고 더듬는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 뉴스나 글에서 '대책을 암중모색하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This is '암중모색' with '-하다', meaning to try various things in search of a way when no clear path is visible. It carries a feeling of groping and uncertainty more than plain '찾다'. It is mostly used in news and writing, as in '대책을 암중모색하다'.

examples.en: That child is small but tough.
The little girl answered in a firm, spirited voice.
She may be short, but she works with grit.
That player fought hard and won the ball.
My younger brother stood up fiercely to his older brother.

examples.ko: 암팡진 성격 덕분에 어려움을 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to her gutsy personality, she overcame the hardship.

explain: 몸집은 작은데 야무지고 당찬 모습에 써요. '야무지다'와 비슷하지만 작은 몸에 비해 힘차다는 느낌이 더 있어요. '암팡지게 달려들다', '암팡진 목소리'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used for someone small in build but firm, capable and spirited. It is similar to '야무지다' but has more of a feeling of being strong for one's small size. Typical uses are '암팡지게 달려들다' and '암팡진 목소리'.
